title: The derived etale sum scalar mate has its degreewise scalar representative
statement: Let e:X→Y be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], A→B a map of commutative rings, and P a bounded complex of flat A-module sheaves on the small etale site of X [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let S_R be exact etale sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], T derived extension of coefficients [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], q_P:T(QP)→Q(P⊗A B) its adjunction-normalized representative [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and t_R:S_R(QP)→Q(S_R P) the exact localization factor. Let σ:S_A⋙T_Y≅T_X⋙S_B be the inverse conjugate of the exact derived restriction/inverse-image square, and let σ⁰ be the ordinary sum/scalar left-adjoint uniqueness comparison as in [lem-sp-etale-sum-coefficient-computation]. Then T_Y(t_A) followed by q_(S_A P) and Q(σ⁰_P) equals σ_(QP) followed by S_B(q_P) and t_B at P⊗A B. This fixes the actual morphisms and needs no flatness of B over A.

source.place: Tag 03S5, sum extension and inverse-image adjunction; more-etale.tex Tag 0GL6, coefficient comparison; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY, left derived functors.

proof.text: Define the comparison of two adjunctions across quotient functors to be the transpose of the localized ordinary unit followed by the inverse right-adjoint factor. Prove directly with homEquiv injectivity and naturality that these comparisons compose. Prove the corresponding compatibility with conjugate transformations by their unit identities. These arguments are formal for arbitrary categories and do not require any representative map to be invertible.

The existing exact-derived adjunction unit formula, transferred from the homotopy quotient to cochain complexes, identifies the comparison for etale sum with its exact localization factor. The definition of scalarExtensionRepresentative identifies the scalar comparison with the same cochain transpose.

The ordinary sum/scalar sheaf isomorphism is leftAdjointUniq, so its unit equation is the ordinary conjugacy equation. Map this equation degreewise. The derived sigma is the inverse adjoint conjugate, hence has the matching derived unit equation. The defining localization-factor formula for mapDerivedCategorySquareIso identifies the right-adjoint square on cochain representatives. Apply the formal comparison compatibility and composition identities to obtain exactly the required equation, without using the supplied degree bounds or flatness hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06YY, cochain scalar transpose normalization, and etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S5. Formal proof using Mathlib adjunction uniqueness and conjugacy, together with the source-library exact-derived unit and localization-factor formulas. No K-flat computation or new intermediate hypothesis.

theorem etaleSumScalarRepresentative
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ⟶ Y) [Etale e]
    (P : CochainComplex (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) ℤ)
    (a b : ℤ) (hz : ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q → IsZero (P.X q))
    (hf : ∀ q : ℤ, exactFunctor _ _ (MonoidalCategory.tensorRight (P.X q))) :
    let σ :
        (etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e inferInstance).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
            scalarExtension φ Y ≅
          scalarExtension φ X ⋙
            (etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) e inferInstance).mapDerivedCategory :=
      ((conjugateIsoEquiv
        ((etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e inferInstance).mapDerivedCategoryAdjunction.comp
          (Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint
            (Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars.{u} Y.smallEtaleTopology φ)))
        ((Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint
            (Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars.{u} X.smallEtaleTopology φ)).comp
          (etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction
            (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) e inferInstance).mapDerivedCategoryAdjunction)).symm
        (Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso
          (upperStarRestrictScalarsIsoSheaf φ e))).symm
    (scalarExtension φ Y).map
        ((etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e inferInstance).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
          P) ≫
      scalarExtensionRepresentative φ Y
        (((etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) e inferInstance).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (etaleSumScalarComplexMap φ e P) =
    σ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
      (etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) e inferInstance).mapDerivedCategory.map
        (scalarExtensionRepresentative φ X P) ≫
      (etaleLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) e inferInstance).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
        (coefficientExtendedComplex φ X P)
